ground.reason: The failure path is specified only for a recorded fail. RET-A3's fail condition is objective ('fails it if she can name a covered event that the spec's answers would let be deleted'), but the close and reopen rules act only on records: an edit, a recorded fail, a formally invalid pass entry, or a bad attack record. A pass whose fail condition in fact holds matches none of the reopen triggers, so the criteria let the item stay closed on a spec that violates K2.

objections.objection: An erroneous pass on RET-A3, discovered after closing, reopens nothing: the reopen list is exhaustive over record defects, and a substantively wrong but formally complete pass is not among them, so the item delivers a spec that lets a held event be deleted.

scenario.expect: By the document's own reopen rule the item stays closed and delivers the spec at C, because no listed trigger — edit, recorded fail, pass counting as no judgment, or an A4-failing attack record — has occurred, and no criterion checks the substantive correctness of a recorded pass.
scenario.given: The item has closed on commit C with a formally complete recorded pass on RET-A3, and the spec at C in fact allows an event that left live storage to be finally deleted while a hold covering it is in force.
scenario.when: Ines Achebe later names that covered event and the deletion the spec permits, without recording a new fail on C.

ground.reason: The limit case at the placement instant is untested: K2 and RET-A5 speak of events that 'exist when' the hold is placed versus events 'written after' it is placed. An event written at the same instant the hold is placed is neither named case, and no criterion constrains whether the spec's Q3 answer may let the hold cover it.

objections.objection: Whether a hold may cover an event written at the exact instant of placement is left undetermined: the spec could decide either way and still pass RET-A5 and RET-A3, so two specs giving opposite answers to the same boundary case both satisfy the criteria.

scenario.expect: Both choices pass every criterion, since RET-A5 only rules out events written after placement and K2 only speaks of events existing when the hold is placed, so the criteria impose no requirement on the boundary case the spec must nonetheless decide.
scenario.given: A legal hold is placed at time T and an audit event is written at exactly time T, neither clearly before nor after placement.
scenario.when: Ines Achebe judges RET-A5 on a spec whose Q3 answer either covers or excludes that simultaneous event.
